title: Design Tokens: The Fastest Way to Stop UI Drift

banner.bannerTitle: Design Tokens: The Fastest Way to Stop UI Drift

intro.introText: A quick refresher on why teams drift into 14 shades of grey and 9 button paddings — and how tokens fix it.

main.heading: Tokens first, overrides last
main.excerpt: We swapped ad-hoc CSS tweaks for semantic tokens and immediately reduced UI inconsistencies across pages.
main.body:
Tokens work best when they’re semantic, not purely visual. Instead of gray-700, think text.primary.

What we shipped

  • Typography + spacing scale
  • Color roles (surface, text, border)
  • Component states (hover, focus, disabled)

Result: fewer one-offs and easier reviews.

blocks.content:
Token naming tip

Use roles like surface.1 and text.muted. It keeps design and code aligned when colors change later.

title: SEO Basics That Still Move the Needle in 2026

banner.bannerTitle: SEO Basics That Still Move the Needle in 2026

intro.introText: No gimmicks: titles, headings, internal links, and clean metadata still win.

main.heading: Clean structure beats clever hacks
main.excerpt: We tightened titles, removed duplicate H1s, and fixed canonical tags across key routes.
main.body:
We focused on a few fundamentals:

  • Unique titles + descriptions per page
  • One clear H1
  • Internal links that match intent

Bonus: better previews via Open Graph tags.

blocks.content:
Mini checklist

  • Title format: primary keyword + outcome
  • Description: 1 sentence + proof/benefit
  • Use descriptive anchor text internally

title: Next.js Performance: Fixing LCP Without Rewriting Everything

banner.bannerTitle: Next.js Performance: Fixing LCP Without Rewriting Everything

intro.introText: We improved perceived speed by prioritising the right assets, not by chasing micro-optimisations.

main.heading: LCP: make the hero show up first
main.excerpt: Priority hints, image sizing, and cutting render-blocking CSS got us most of the win.
main.body:
We tackled LCP by making sure the hero content loads early and stays stable:

  • Reserved layout space to avoid CLS
  • Reduced render-blocking work
  • Kept client-side JS lean on landing pages

title: Security Quick Wins for Web Apps (That Don’t Hurt DX)

banner.bannerTitle: Security Quick Wins for Web Apps (That Don’t Hurt DX)

intro.introText: A few guardrails: safer headers, better validation, and rate limiting where it matters.

main.heading: Safer by default
main.excerpt: We added stricter server validation and protected public endpoints from spam bursts.
main.body:
We focused on boring-but-effective measures:

  • Server-side validation (always)
  • Basic rate limiting on forms
  • Sanitised output where user content renders

It’s not glamorous, but it’s reliable.

blocks.content:
Rule of thumb

If it can be triggered by the public internet, it needs validation, throttling, and logging.

title: Rebuilding a Navigation: From “Everything Everywhere” to Clear IA

banner.bannerTitle: Rebuilding a Navigation: From “Everything Everywhere” to Clear IA

intro.introText: We simplified the site nav, reduced cognitive load, and improved findability for key pages.

main.heading: Fewer choices, faster decisions
main.excerpt: A smaller primary nav + clearer labels improves both UX and internal link structure.
main.body:
We cut the primary nav down to the essentials and moved secondary items into contextual menus.

Unexpected win: cleaner internal linking helped SEO signals as well.

blocks.content:
IA tip

If a label needs a tooltip, it’s probably not a good label. Use plain language and common terms.

title: Accessibility Pass: Focus Rings, Contrast, and Keyboard Paths

banner.bannerTitle: Accessibility Pass: Focus Rings, Contrast, and Keyboard Paths

intro.introText: We did a quick accessibility sweep: focus visibility, contrast, and ‘can you use it without a mouse?’

main.heading: Keyboard-first checks catch real bugs
main.excerpt: A simple tab-through pass found missing focus states and broken modal traps in minutes.
main.body:
We checked:

  • Focus order (does it make sense?)
  • Focus visibility (is it obvious?)
  • Modal traps and escape behaviour

Small fixes, big UX improvement.

title: Refactoring CSS: From “Utility Soup” to Intentional Layouts

banner.bannerTitle: Refactoring CSS: From “Utility Soup” to Intentional Layouts

intro.introText: Utilities are great until nobody knows what anything does. We introduced patterns for layout and spacing.

main.heading: Layouts should be readable
main.excerpt: We kept utilities, but added layout primitives so the DOM is easier to scan and maintain.
main.body:
We introduced a small set of layout components/patterns: containers, stacks, clusters, and grids.

That reduced repeated class chains and made spacing changes safer.

blocks.content:
Keep it simple

A layout system should be small enough to remember. If it needs a handbook, it’s too big.

title: Build Pipeline Cleanup: Faster CI With Less Noise

banner.bannerTitle: Build Pipeline Cleanup: Faster CI With Less Noise

intro.introText: We removed redundant steps, improved caching, and made failures clearer so they’re faster to fix.

main.heading: CI should be boring
main.excerpt: Less waiting, fewer flaky jobs, and clearer logs for front-end builds.
main.body:
We focused on repeatability:

  • Cache dependencies
  • Split lint/test/build stages
  • Fail fast on formatting + types

blocks.content:
Small win

Make logs readable. If the error is buried, it costs time every single PR.

title: Structured Content: Designing Blocks That Editors Actually Use

banner.bannerTitle: Structured Content: Designing Blocks That Editors Actually Use

intro.introText: We tested content blocks with real editing flows: less flexibility, more consistency, faster publishing.

main.heading: Flexible, but not chaotic
main.excerpt: A couple of well-designed blocks can cover 90% of use cases and keep pages consistent.
main.body:
We kept two blocks: rich text and image galleries. Then we documented patterns like:

  • Intro → Gallery → Details
  • Problem → Solution → Proof

Editors ship faster when the structure is clear.

blocks.content:
Editor-friendly rule

If a block needs a training session, it’s too complex. Keep options minimal and outcomes predictable.

title: Hardening a Marketing Site: Practical Security for Public Pages

banner.bannerTitle: Hardening a Marketing Site: Practical Security for Public Pages

intro.introText: Even “just a brochure site” can get abused. We locked down forms, headers, and embed behaviour.

main.heading: Protect the edges
main.excerpt: We focused on the obvious entry points: forms, third-party embeds, and unsafe defaults.
main.body:
We implemented basic hardening:

  • Safer response headers
  • Form throttling + validation
  • Audit of third-party scripts

Low effort, high return.
